changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 5 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6329-actionparam-one-authority.md`

- names `ActionPreview.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/ActionPreview.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `ActionParam` has one authority again (objectui#6329). The name was declared three times, not twice as the card counted: `@object-ui/types` publishes it — derived from the spec's `ActionParamSchema` input, with its own parity suite — and `ActionDefaultInspector.tsx` and `ActionPreview.tsx` each carried a module-local `interface` of the same name. app-shell already read the published one elsewhere (`utils/resolveActionParams.test.ts`), so both locals were shadows. They are deleted, not reconciled against each other, under the 2026-08-25 family ruling 甲A1.

### `.changeset/7298-discussion-explicit-composition.md`

- names `content/docs/guide/slotted-pages.md` → `content/docs/guide/slotted-pages.md` — edited by this change

  > Docs: `content/docs/guide/slotted-pages.md`.

### `.changeset/8649-detail-renderer-undeclared-keys.md`

- names `record-related-list.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-related-list.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **`@object-ui/plugin-detail` — the annotation-erasing destructure default is gone from three renderers.** `record-details.tsx`, `record-highlights.tsx` and `record-related-list.tsx` each annotated `schema` correctly and then wrote `schema = {} as any`. A destructuring default's type joins the annotated property type at the binding, so `any` erased the annotation for *every* read site in the file — declared keys and undeclared ones alike read `any`. No published surface moves: the exported annotations were always correct.

### `.changeset/9964-related-list-picker-filter-mirror.md`

- names `record-related-list.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-related-list.tsx` — edited by this change

  > So one key carried two declarations, with the looser one on the face an author — or an AI writing metadata — reads: `unknown` offers no shape guidance for a key whose consumer demands a specific shape. Nothing could report the divergence either, because `record-related-list.tsx` reached the block through four `(schema as any).add` reads; a cast unwraps the declaration at its own read site, so no compiler ever compared the two.

### `.changeset/plugin-detail-8937-parent-scope-residue.md`

- names `RelatedList.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx` — edited by this change

  > - **`packages/plugin-detail/README.md` (it is in `files[]`, so it ships).** It said the node's `filter` is AND-combined with `{ [relationshipField]: parentId }`, full stop. Since objectui#7299 the parent condition is compiled to match the relationship field's arity, so a multi-valued relationship gets `{ [relationshipField]: { $contains: parentId } }` instead. The paragraph now states both spellings and names the arbiter (`@objectstack/spec/data`'s `isMultiValueField`). - **The claim that the SQL driver decides arity on that same predicate.** It does not: `driver-sql` gates the equality family on its own storage question, which reads `multiple` as truthy on ANY type. The two rules therefore disagree for a type outside `MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES` carrying `multiple: true`. objectui#9184 moved the arity compiler into `@object-ui/core`'s `parent-scope` seam and carried the claim with it, so the correction is recorded there — the seam now states the driver's measured rule, records the divergence as a divergence, and points at the upstream card that owns which of the two rules is right (objectstack#17469). `RelatedList.tsx`'s pointer comment and the objectui#7299 test header carried the same sentence and are corrected to match.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `1b30c0fe0` (merge-base with origin/main): 11 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1855 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2467 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36792150634)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b04aaba6d21abf6bc8b3de572bf5637a1bffc13d`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and nothing else: card #11270 (body; comments `5919760660` unlock, `5920436535` cross-lane note, `5920737104` claim, `5921704724` dev report); PR #11289 (body, 12-file list, the net diff from merge-base `e420df310f` to the head: 4 commits, +686/−43); the check-runs on the head (read twice); triage's enforce answer objectstack-ai/objectstack#20937 `5919625056`; objectstack `origin/main` `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` and `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`, read-only. Not the dispatch order, not the seat's conclusions. Nothing built, run or re-run; the dev's red-first, ablation and suite figures are quoted from the report where named and are not re-derived here.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The placement — right, and the negative is pinned.**
- `deriveActions` now takes `locations: readonly ActionLocation[]` and keeps a child action when any surface location passes `actionRendersAt`, the platform's one placement rule. One pass over `childDef.actions`, so an action declaring both `list_item` and `record_related` renders once, in the child's declared order (pinned by `archive` in the bridge pin, expected order `send_reminder`, `log_time`, `archive`).
- The row set is `ROW_LOCATIONS_IN_RECORD` (`list_item`, `record_related`) only when `hasParentRecord` holds (`parentRecordId` non-null and non-empty), else `ROW_LOCATIONS` (`list_item`); `hasParentRecord` joins the `useMemo` dependency list. The toolbar reads `TOOLBAR_LOCATIONS` (`list_toolbar`) alone, unchanged. The one production mount is `RecordDetailView`, which passes `parentRecordId` from the route's record id.
- The child's own list view is untouched: `ObjectView`'s `rowActionDefs` still filters on `locations.includes('list_item')`, and the list page's `listRecordActionsValue` still resolves `NO_RELATED_HANDLERS`, so a related list under a list page gets no row actions.
- This is the enforce answer: each row of the related list, only inside a parent record, never on the object's own list views — the words objectstack `action.zod.ts` now carries on `origin/main` (PR 20948), and consistent with the runtime's `requiresRecord`, which counts `record_related` beside `list_item`, `record_header` and `record_more`.
- The negative is pinned twice: `ObjectView.recordRelatedNotOnOwnList-11270.test.tsx` (`log_time` absent while `send_reminder` and `archive` are present over the same render) and the bridge pin's parent-less mount (`send_reminder`, `archive` only). Red-first commit `7c50fdac8a` precedes the implementation on the branch.
- Observation, not this PR's: `ObjectView.rowActionDefs` still reads `locations.includes` directly rather than `actionRendersAt` — the same declared-only semantics, a pre-existing dialect the bridge no longer shares.

**(b) The file-surface correction — inside the claim's intent; the doc-only additions are in scope.**
- No `RelatedRecordActionsBridge*` exists under `packages/plugin-detail/src` at the merge-base or the head. The bridge is `packages/app-shell/src/views/RelatedRecordActionsBridge.tsx`. The card body itself placed it in `packages/plugin-detail` and the claim inherited that path; the claim's object — `deriveActions` and its behaviour — is what changed. A corrected address, not corrected work; reported as deviation 1. `@object-ui/app-shell` therefore carries the bridge and the preview.
- The doc-only additions each correct a statement the diff would have made false: `RelatedRecordHandlers.rowActions` in `@object-ui/react` (public through `context/index.ts`) said `locations: ['list_item']`; `RelatedListProps.rowActions` and the composition-rule docblock in `record-related-list.tsx` said the same; `content/docs/guide/slotted-pages.md` said "declared with `locations: ['list_item']` in each row's menu" and "declares neither `list_toolbar` nor `list_item`". objectui AGENTS.md #2 (Docs-driven: "Not done until docs reflect the code") makes the guide edit owed, not optional. The three package READMEs (`plugin-detail`, `app-shell`, `react`) carry no location-set wording, so nothing else was owed. In scope.

**(c) The authored channel — PR objectui#11263's composition rule extended, not changed.**
- `placeAuthoredRelatedListActions`: `onToolbar` unchanged; `onRow` is now `list_item` or `record_related` through `actionRendersAt`; an id is refused only when none of the three holds. One loop, authored order, the `seen` dedupe, all unchanged. The rule (ABSENT: the host's actions untouched; AUTHORED: the authored list, each id placed by its own `locations`; unplaceable REFUSED, never drawn elsewhere or dropped) is intact; the row surface's location set grew by one member.
- `describeRelatedListActionRefusals` names `list_toolbar (header)`, `list_item (row menu)` and `record_related (row menu inside a record)`. Pinned on the pure function and through the real renderer (`record-related-list-actions-refused`), with the placeable sibling still rendering.
- The channel gates `record_related` on nothing; its ground is that `record:related_list` only ever draws inside a parent record. Verified: the block takes its parent link value from `useRecordContext()`; without a record context the value is null and `RelatedList` does not fetch. So the two channels answer "inside a record" by different facts — the bridge by its `parentRecordId` prop, the block by its identity — and at the product's one mount both hold together. Observation, not blocking.
- `relatedListActions.ts` is module-internal (imported only by `record-related-list.tsx`; absent from `index.tsx`'s export list), so the changed notice text and the `PlacedRelatedListActions` doc are not public API.

**(d) `ActionPreview` — the smallest change, and it matches the product.**
- The two-row element `list_item` drew is hoisted to `rows` and reused: `list_item` keeps it; `record_section` keeps its header frame, now alone; `record_related` gets its own `Frame` over `rows`. No new frame family, no new i18n key (`engine.actionPreview.placement.row` reused; `check:i18n-dead-keys` clean per the report). The header button for `record_related` — the reading the ruling replaced — is gone.
- Side-correction, accepted as within the cross-lane note's intent: at the base, declaring both `record_section` and `record_related` drew ONE frame captioned `record_related` and hid `record_section`'s. Now each draws its own; pinned ("each draw their own frame").
- The rows are generic under the `record_related` caption; the inspector's location label `engine.inspector.action.location.record_related` ("Record · related list") carries the scope. Adequate.

**Readers of `record_related`, at the merge-base and the head.** At the base: the preview's header frame, the inspector label map, `block-config.ts`'s option list, i18n strings and an `action-bar.tsx` docblock — none a placement, so the card's premise held. At the head the only placements are the bridge and the authored channel; nothing else moved.

**Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each named:**
1. `record:related_list.actions` (authored): an id whose action declares `record_related` and neither other related-list location was REFUSED with a notice; it is now placed on each row. Widening. Right.
2. The console record page: a child action declaring `record_related` rendered nowhere; it is now in each related-list row's menu, beside `list_item`. Widening of what the host honours. Right.
3. The designer preview: `record_related` draws rows, not a section header. Right.
4. Nothing narrows: `list_item`, `list_toolbar`, `record_section`, the child's own list view, the built-in Edit / Delete affordances and the row visibility gate are unchanged or comment-only. No export is added or removed in `plugin-detail` (`index.tsx` untouched), `react` (`RelatedRecordHandlers` shape unchanged) or `app-shell` (`index.ts` untouched).

**Check-runs on the head.** At the first read, 11 runs were in progress. At the second read, 2026-09-30T23:49:44Z: 32 `success`, 3 `skipped` (the path-conditional coverage shards and dependabot), 7 `in_progress` — `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Test (shard 1/8)`, `2/8`, `4/8`, `6/8`, `7/8`, `8/8`. Those seven are NOT CONCLUDED and are not read here as pass or fail. Concluded `success` include `Lint`, `Type Check`, `Test (shard 3/8)`, `Test (shard 5/8)`, `Test (dist pins)`, `Build & E2E`, `Live E2E (informational)`, `Build Docs`, `Doc Snippet Type Check`, `Doc Component Type Check`, `Doc Fence Language Check`, `Doc Example Id Check`, `Internal Docs Link Check`, the five `Changeset` runs, `Line Citation Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Pre-Install Import Graph Check`. (h): `Doc Snippet Type Check` concluded `success` on this head; the guide diff touches two prose paragraphs and two bullets, and its one fenced block is unchanged context — so the local NOT MEASURED on `check:doc-snippets` / `check:doc-examples` is closed by the check-run.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/11270-record-related-row-placement.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell` minor, `@object-ui/plugin-detail` minor, `@object-ui/react` patch.
